what happened: gdbmtool(1) does not list the recover command, and GDBM's own manual (the Texinfo one, with the recovery and crash-tolerance chapters) is not installed. I took the recovery path from `gdbmtool help` and from what I know of that manual
the command or file that showed it: man gdbmtool; gdbmtool -N -q x.db help; ls /usr/share/info

what happened: The define directory has to stay flat, but sideeye's state must be a directory, so the state lives outside it at ../state
gdbmtool exits 0 when a command fails (missing key, missing file, bad magic). The checker and recover.sh treat any stderr text as failure

With GDBM's default mmap, preflight refused state_changed_without_ops: writes into the mapping are not recorded operations. The operation now runs gdbmtool -m (--no-mmap), so the mmap path is untested
A ';' in the string-form operation drew a shell-syntax warning (it is gdbmtool's own separator, passed as written). I switched to the argv form

gdbmtool recover prints 'Recovery succeeded' and exits 0 even when it drops every record (bucket header damaged at offset 8192 -> empty db). Its message cannot be trusted; the checker judges the records after it
the command or file that showed it: dd seek=8192 over a copy of db.gdbm; gdbmtool -N -q c.gdbm recover verbose summary; gdbmtool -N -q -r c.gdbm list

what happened: No explored world needs recovery: each kill lands before a call, and each store's bucket is one 4096-byte write. To show an accepted recovered state, I searched one-byte damage offsets for one that recover fully repairs (4096). Only that hand-made state exercises recover.sh
The first run-controls.sh marked all three valid states WRONG although check.sh exited 0: an && / || precedence mistake in the runner, not in the checker
Control a cannot break leg a and literally no other: an unreadable database leaves b-e with nothing to judge. The checker prints '-' (not judged) for them rather than FAIL
